At the pinned commit (23adee04) fit_spiral.py is a headless CLI over a service-oriented rewrite: three flags (--dataset, --scroll-spec, --cache), the scroll's identity read from a spiral-scroll.json manifest at the dataset root, and everything else -- around 120 keys, including the z range and the optimizer seed -- through FIT_SPIRAL_CONFIG_OVERRIDES, validated against upstream's Config class.

The scroll's name, voxel size and winding sense are no longer module constants assigned at import (that mechanism, and the AST rebind this adapter used to drive it, existed only at the previously pinned commit, 05dcf034). They are spiral-scroll.json fields; the adapter writes that manifest fresh for every run, atomically, and reads it back before the run is allowed to start. spiral_outward_sense is CW or ACW there; this platform keeps CW/CCW as its own public vocabulary and translates CCW to ACW at that one boundary.

The adapter imports upstream's lightweight config.py directly to get the accepted override keys, rather than parsing fit_spiral.py's own AST as before -- config.py does no dataset I/O, unlike fit_spiral.py, whose module level opens Zarr groups -- and rejects an unknown override before a GPU is claimed instead of after.

The fit itself is checkpoint-centric now: a run writes checkpoint_fitted.ckpt and stops. Getting a surface out of it is a second subprocess, upstream's own flatten_spiral_checkpoint.py, which reconstructs the combined spiral surface and flattens it through a private Lasagna service. Both subprocesses run from the P1 queue on the spiral-fit lane, through framework/stages/01-segmentation/scripts/run_spiral_fit.py, in helena-villa-python -- the image that carries spiral-fitting/ and lasagna/. helena-villa is compiled binaries and cannot run either; a worker in the wrong runtime refuses by name before the lease.

The exported surface is published to the fleet's artifact store and registered with import_surface, the same route a grown surface takes, so P2's geometry certification and the lamina gate apply unchanged. One fit now produces one surface (a combined, flattened range of windings), not one TIFXYZ per winding as at the previous pin.

spiral-fitter-v1@0.4.1 (framework/profiles/01-segmentation/spiral-fitter-v1-0.4.1.json) is a sibling of spiral-fitter-v1@0.4.0 on the same spiral-fit lane, turning patches back on (input_disable_patches: false, input_use_verified_patches: false, consuming grown, unverified track-graph patches instead) so an A/B against the minimal, patch-less route is possible. Neither profile supersedes the other.

input_contract.input: an already-staged scroll's own tracks/{tracks_file} DBM -- the same file a spiral fit reads
input_contract.output: one .tifxyz patch per grown seed, written into the dataset's own unverified_patches_dir
input_contract.surface_prior: graph-topological growth over the track graph's own crossings, from an explicit or random seed row

notes: The published verified_patches villa ships (PHercParis4's own examples) are for a scroll ineligible for this campaign's targets. Villa's own recipe for growing patches on a different, already-tracked scroll is VC3D's GUI action 'Actions > Grow track patches', which blocks any queued or automated use.

grow_track_graph.py, in the same pinned spiral-fitting/ package spiral-fitter runs, already has a complete headless argparse CLI -- confirmed by reading the file directly, not assumed from upstream's GUI action. Three scripts bridge what this platform stages to what that CLI wants: convert_track_store.py packs tracks/{tracks_file} (the same DBM load_tracks_from_dbm opens) into a memory-mapped .vctracks store; build_track_crossings.py indexes the same DBM into an exact-crossing CSR sidecar, with source_ids aligned to the packed store by construction (both walk sorted(dbm.keys()) the same way over the same file); grow_track_graph.py reads both and writes one TIFXYZ per grown seed. No step is GUI-only or shells out to a compiled VC3D binary -- confirmed by reading every import in all three files and the two tracks.py functions they call.

Needs no GPU: none of the three scripts, nor the two tracks.py functions they call, perform a CUDA operation. tracks.py imports torch/kornia at module level for code elsewhere in that file, so the subprocess needs an interpreter where torch is importable (helena-villa-python already is one), but no worker needs a card claimed to run it. Registered on the P1 queue's grow-track-patches lane with gpu_required: false, guarded by test_a_lane_asks_for_a_card_only_if_it_uses_one.py's own generic coverage.

Output is deliberately routed as unverified_patches, not verified_patches: nothing in this pipeline attaches a human review, and spiral-fitting's own FIT_INPUT_CATALOG treats the two very differently (verified_patches is required the instant it is enabled and gates abs_winding.json's absolute-winding annotations; unverified_patches is masked against trusted geometry and never required). Not registered as a surface of its own -- no import_surface call -- because a grown patch is an input to a future fit, not a certified artifact.
entries.recommended_policy: Run only ahead of a spiral-fitter-v1@0.4.1 fit that names the same --unverified-patches-dir; this method does not decide whether patches help (a villa contributor separately reported track-graph patches as 'currently strangely unhelpful in the spiral' on this kind of geometry) -- it makes that comparison measurable, and measures nothing on its own.

identity_policy: A method name is descriptive only. Execution identity requires source revision, checkpoint SHA-256 when applicable, preprocessing contract, physical voxel scale, coordinate/layer order, and adapter version.
